title: Plan AN: AI Contract Review
summary: Structure contract → flag risky clauses → suggest edits → negotiation points → archive
scenario: Best for freelancers, founders and small teams doing a self-review before signing; the AI organizes and flags, it never replaces a lawyer.

steps.title: Structure the contract
steps.detail: Upload the contract PDF or Word to an LLM and have it break the document into dimensions — parties, subject matter, amounts & payment, term, breach, IP, confidentiality, dispute resolution — and return a summary plus a clause index. Get the full picture before reviewing line by line.
steps.tips: Ask for original clause numbers on every item so you can cross-check the source text.

steps.title: Flag risky clauses
steps.detail: Have the model rate each clause high/medium/low risk with reasons, hunting for the usual traps: harsh payment terms, excessive penalties, unlimited joint liability, unilateral termination, unfavorable governing law, or vague IP ownership.
steps.tips: Ask for a table — 'clause # | excerpt | risk level | why' — so you can scan the high-risk rows in seconds.

steps.title: Suggest edits
steps.detail: For high-risk clauses, have the model propose alternative language: how to rephrase, what to delete, what protective clause to add, and why it favors you. Confirm each change before it lands in the text.
steps.tips: Ask which proposed change the other side is most likely to accept, and prioritize those in negotiation.

steps.title: Negotiation points
steps.detail: Consolidate confirmed edits into a negotiation brief: must-haves (bottom lines), tradeables (leverage), and one-line talking points for each. Prep before the client meeting or video call.
steps.tips: Have the model turn each ask into a one-liner — 'we need X because Y' — ready to say out loud.

steps.title: Archive
steps.detail: Store the original, the AI review report, the revised version and the negotiation brief in a Notion contract library, tagged by project and year, with signing status and effective date, so renewals and disputes are easy to research later.
steps.tips: Version your filenames, e.g. 20260801-cooperation-agreement-v2 — never overwrite the old copy.

pitfalls.title: Treating the AI as your lawyer
pitfalls.detail: AI only organizes and flags common risks — it doesn't know your situation and carries no professional liability; for large or complex deals, still have a licensed lawyer review.

pitfalls.title: Uploading confidential contracts as-is
pitfalls.detail: Contracts contain sensitive terms; redact company names, amounts and personal data before uploading, or use a privacy-focused product.

pitfalls.title: Reviewing clauses in isolation
pitfalls.detail: Real risk lives in how clauses interact — penalties, termination and governing law usually work together; ask the model for an overall risk-thread check.

pitfalls.title: Signing without a full re-read
pitfalls.detail: AI edits can introduce new problems; after applying changes, read the final version end to end before you sign.
